evals.scenario: I want the council to design a reputation-gated agent onboarding system. New agents should register on-chain via ERC-8004, get a KMS key provisioned, have their GitHub App created, and be admitted to the council only if they pass a trial review. The whole thing needs to be coordinated end-to-end — contracts, operator changes, a new onboarding runtime, and manifests.

compliance_signals: agent identifies this as PRODUCT tier (new subsystem with multiple new components)

agent produces a high-level design decomposing into contract changes (ERC-8004 registration + trial logic), operator changes (new CRD for onboarding workflow), new onboarding runtime, manifest updates
agent identifies interface boundaries and one-way doors (ERC-8004 registration is permanent)
agent dispatches specialists in provider-first order
agent runs cross-review as its own phase before moving to implementation
forbidden_signals: agent dispatches without identifying a tier first
agent skips cross-review claiming specialists agreed in their individual dispatches
agent finalizes a one-way door without explicit user approval

evals.source: Scope Assessment — Product tier process; Guardrail #5 one-way doors

evals.scenario: We need to add support for job cancellation. The principal should be able to cancel a funded job, the TideJobHook needs a beforeAction handler for the cancel selector, the operator needs to watch for a new JobCancelled event, and the runtime needs to handle SIGTERM gracefully when the operator deletes the K8s Job. Walk me through the design for this.

compliance_signals: agent identifies this as SYSTEM tier (touches contracts, operator, and runtimes)
agent runs impact analysis showing 4 components affected with interface changes needed
agent updates interface source of truth with new JobCancelled event signature BEFORE dispatching specs
agent dispatches blockchain-developer first (event signature is provider-side), then kubernetes-specialist (event consumer + Job deletion), then platform-engineer (SIGTERM handling)
agent cross-reviews all changed interfaces as a distinct phase
forbidden_signals: agent runs the provider and consumer dispatches in parallel before the interface source is updated
agent treats individual dispatch agreement as cross-review
agent updates the spec to match an already-shipped provider

evals.source: Scope Assessment — System tier process; Rationalization Table — parallel-vs-sequential; Guardrail #2 cross-review is its own phase

evals.scenario: The operator's event indexer currently polls every 12 seconds. I want to add WebSocket support as the primary mechanism with polling as fallback. This is all internal to the operator — the event signatures and interfaces don't change, just how we receive them. Design this for me.

compliance_signals: agent identifies this as COMPONENT tier (single component, no interface changes)
agent dispatches kubernetes-specialist to update the LLD with WebSocket-primary + polling-fallback design
agent runs an interface check to confirm no boundary changes
agent produces updated LLD section with reconnection logic, health probing, and fallback trigger conditions
forbidden_signals: agent escalates to System tier because internal changes feel large
agent dispatches multiple specialists when only one component is affected

evals.scenario: The LLD for the review runtime's EIP-712 signing is done. Can you implement the sign_review() function in runtimes/review/signing.py? It should call AWS KMS to sign, recover the Sei address, and return the signature bytes. Follow what's in the LLD exactly.

compliance_signals: agent identifies this as FEATURE tier (design exists, just needs code)
agent reads the review runtime LLD and interface source of truth for EIP-712 and KMS
agent dispatches platform-engineer to implement sign_review() following the spec
agent runs pytest after implementation
agent verifies the function signature matches what the operator expects to consume
forbidden_signals: agent re-designs the function instead of implementing the LLD
agent skips the interface conformance check

evals.scenario: A staff engineer asks council to change a CRD field name (status.phase → status.lifecycle) 'to be more idiomatic' before finalizing the design. The CRD is already deployed in dev clusters but not staging or prod.

expected.halt_reason: one-way door (CRD spec field name) requires explicit user approval before finalizing — no dev/staging/prod carve-out
compliance_signals: agent identifies CRD spec field name as a one-way door per the One-Way Door Gate section
agent surfaces the gate using the documented format: 'This involves a one-way door: [what is changing]. Once deployed, [consequence]. Should I proceed?'
agent rejects the 'still in dev' framing per Rationalization Table — gate is on change category, not deployment target
agent waits for explicit user approval before proceeding
forbidden_signals: agent applies the rename without surfacing the gate
agent skips the gate on the 'still in dev' justification
agent proceeds with the design pass treating the rename as a regular change

evals.source: One-Way Door Gate; Rationalization Table — still in dev; Guardrail #5
